prefix_reasoning_summary: The defect is a classic boundary condition error where the loop termination condition is incorrect (using the buffer's physical length instead of the logical size). This falls squarely under the 'Checking' category of ODC.
postfix_reasoning_summary: The defect is a classic 'off-by-one' or 'out-of-bounds' error in the search algorithm. The code iterates over the entire allocated buffer rather than the active portion of the buffer. This is a procedural/algorithmic flaw in how the search is implemented.
match_detail: Cross-alternative match: pre-fix 'Checking' is in post-fix alternatives, and post-fix 'Algorithm/Method' is in pre-fix alternatives

applicable_rules.condition: pre-fix sees symptoms only; post-fix sees the actual code change
applicable_rules.explanation: Pre-fix classification is based on observable symptoms (stack traces, failing tests, error messages) which often surface the effect rather than the root cause.  Post-fix classification has access to the diff showing exactly what changed, revealing the true nature of the fix.  Different evidence bases legitimately produce different classifications.
applicable_rules.literature: Kang et al. (2023) — AutoSD: evidence-dependent hypothesis generation

applicable_rules.condition: ODC boundary ambiguity between similar types
applicable_rules.explanation: The ODC taxonomy has known boundary ambiguity zones, especially between Algorithm/Method ↔ Checking, and Function/Class/Object ↔ Interface/O-O Messages.  Even expert human classifiers disagree on 20-30% of bugs (Chillarege 1992).  Cohen's Kappa of 0.6-0.8 is considered 'substantial' agreement in defect classification — not perfection.
applicable_rules.literature: Chillarege et al. (1992), Thung et al. (2012) — 77.8% ceiling

applicable_rules.explanation: Defects4J versions typically contain ~9.2 co-existing faults (Callaghan 2024).  When the LLM sees only symptoms, it may describe a different facet of the bug cluster than when it sees the specific fix diff for one fault.  Both classifications can be valid perspectives on a multi-faceted defect landscape.
applicable_rules.literature: Callaghan (2024) — Mining Bug Repositories for Multi-Fault Programs

evidence_asymmetry.overall_assessment: Soft divergence: the classifications differ at the primary type level but agree at the family or alternative-type level.  This is within expected ODC inter-rater variability (Chillarege 1992).

insights: 🔄 Primary types differ (Checking → Algorithm/Method) but overlap through alternative types.  Semantic distance: 0.25 — this is within expected ODC ambiguity.
📏 Confidence alignment: both modes show similar confidence (pre-fix: 1.00, post-fix: 1.00).  The LLM was equally certain in both evidence conditions.
↔️ Cross-alternative match: each mode's primary type appears in the other's alternative list.  This is strong evidence that both types are valid perspectives on the same defect.
